title: Amino acid metabolism during prolonged starvation
authors: Felig P, Owen OE, Wahren J, Cahill GF Jr
population: Nine obese adults studied during 13 periods of starvation of 21 to 42 days, and eight patients undergoing diagnostic cardiac catheterisation after a 12 to 14 h fast (five) or a 36 to 48 h fast (three)
funder: This work was supported in part by U. S. Public Health Service Grants AM-05077, AM-09584, AM-09748, HE-05679, HE-08591, HE-11306, and FR-31, and the John H. Hartford Foundation, Inc., New York. P. Felig held a U. S. Public Health Service Special Postdoctoral Fellowship, 5-F3-AM-36-069.
result: In all subjects the splanchnic circulation extracted more alanine than all other amino acids combined. After a 36 to 48 h fast, fractional splanchnic extraction of alanine rose from 43% to 71% without a significant change in arterial alanine. During prolonged starvation plasma alanine fell by 70% while total alpha-amino nitrogen fell 12%; after 5 to 6 weeks splanchnic alanine uptake fell because of the lower arterial concentration, and the kidney took up glycine and alanine.
